spec_match.rationale: Tests the WebIDL consequences the spec implies: reliability as a getter-only accessor on the prototype, supportsReliableOnly as a static accessor on the constructor, strict-mode write TypeError, and statics not reaching instances.

interactive.rationale: Two buttons run real descriptor dumps and three real strict-mode assignments against a live transport object, with per-row expected/unexpected coloring and polite summaries.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises descriptor dumps, the throwing write, the undefined instance lookup, and the unknown-enum stance; all four are on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: The absent-feature branch is first-class: the page explains that a strict write succeeding (creating an expando) is itself evidence, and cleans up the constructor property it creates; the recorded three-engines table is explicitly labelled documentation, not a live probe.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus, the supportsReliableOnly spec anchor, and WebIDL's static-attributes section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's descriptor-shape, strict-write-throws, and static-placement assertions encode exactly this page's checks; executes honestly as 1 pass / 7 fail / 1 blocked on Chromium 141.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this environment): dump and write buttons driven on desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740, zero console errors, zero failed requests, 0px overflow, screenshots read — descriptor rows honestly read "nowhere", writes table showed the expected absent-feature outcomes. Partial: the TypeError-throwing path needs a 158+ build.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts descriptor shape and write semantics with expected-vs-observed payloads; the expando created on the constructor during the absent-branch test is deleted immediately.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; emerald/rose verdict cells sit on bg-paper; buttons set background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Captioned tables with row/column th scope, native buttons, one polite output per panel, and outcome rows carry full text (not color-only).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800 with 0px horizontal overflow; long monospace identifiers wrap via word-break; both screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Confirm the TypeError rows on a 158+ build
openQuestions.detail: On Chromium 141 all three writes exercise the absent-feature expectations. On a Chrome 158+ or WebTransportReliability-flagged build, re-run "the writes that must fail" and confirm rows 1 and 2 report TypeError and row 3 still reads undefined, and that the descriptor table's "matches the IDL?" column goes green.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive comparison table narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Semantic tables with proper header scope inside an overflow wrapper; wrap long tokens.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All three tables use caption + th scope in .table-wrap; row-header identifiers use word-break:break-all so the 49-char member names cannot force overflow at 360px (measured 0px).

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for async API probe result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: One polite live region per surface, meaningful announcements only, never color as the only signal.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each panel has exactly one aria-live output written once per action with the final summary; every colored cell also carries the full outcome text.

summary: Descriptor dumps, strict-mode writes, and the static-vs-instance lookup, all run against live objects, with an explicitly-labelled recorded engines table. Verified with the repo headless-Chromium CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment) on Chromium 141: honest absent-feature outcomes throughout, clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
